title: Read a submit command
prompt: This program writes a small job and submits it with `spark-submit`. It prints the exit code, then the lines the job printed, without their `app:` prefix. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
import os, subprocess

open("/tmp/job.py", "w").write("""
import sys
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = (SparkSession.builder
         .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2")
         .getOrCreate())
sc = spark.sparkContext
print("app:", sc.appName)
print("app:", sc.master, sc.defaultParallelism)
print("app:", spark.conf.get("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions"))
print("app:", sys.argv[1:])
spark.stop()
""")

env = {**os.environ, "SPARK_LOCAL_IP": "127.0.0.1"}
run = subprocess.run(
    ["spark-submit", "--master", "local[3]", "--name", "hourly-errors",
     "--conf", "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=6",
     "/tmp/job.py", "2026-02-01", "checkout-api"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
print(run.returncode)
for line in run.stdout.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("app:"):
        print(line[5:])
hints: `--name` and `--master` set the application name and the master; `local[3]` means 3 cores, and `defaultParallelism` follows the cores.
The job's builder sets the shuffle partitions too. Which wins: the code or `--conf`?
Only the words after the script's path reach `sys.argv[1:]`.
